Maya: heads-up — after the Node 18 roll yesterday the background-batcher service is showing a bunch of traces with only the entry span. child spans (kv.cache.*) are missing for ~25% of requests. trace id: 4a1f2d3c... anyone seen this pattern?

Ben: are these all coming from the new worker thread pool? link to a sample trace: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/trace/4a1f2d3c

Lee: quick checklist — 1) collector sampling? 2) propagators mismatch? 3) context manager (async_hooks) in OTEL JS. can you paste the collector sampling config?

Maya: collector shows 1% tail-sampling + 100% parent-based in agent — looks fine. here's the service env: `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=background-batcher`, `OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage`, Node is 18.17.0. logs show this when spans are missing:
```
[batcher] start child span kv.get key=foo
... later nothing, parent finished
```

Sam: we've seen async_hooks regressions on Node 18 minor. If you use `@opentelemetry/context-async-hooks` make sure its version matches API. try forcing context manager enable in bootstrap:
```
const { AsyncHooksContextManager } = require('@opentelemetry/context-async-hooks');
const ctxManager = new AsyncHooksContextManager();
ctxManager.enable();
api.context.setGlobalContextManager(ctxManager);
```

Ben: also check if some code uses `setImmediate`/`worker_threads` and doesn't propagate context — instrumentation doesn't automatically patch custom threads.

Maya: good call — batcher spawns a few worker_threads for parsing. i'll instrument the worker start to propagate context using `parentSpan.spanContext()` and `propagation.inject`. trying now.

oncall-bot: deploy finished background-batcher@2026-03-16T10:12:34Z :rocket:

Lee: if still flaky try running the collector locally and tail incoming spans: `otelcol --config config.yaml` or curl the OTLP endpoint:
```
curl -X POST http://collector.internal:4318/v1/traces -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @sample.json
```

Maya: ok will test with worker context injection + bump context lib to latest. if it persists i'll paste a short trace id and sample logs. thanks. :thumbsup:
